To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a conformational analysis of the nine cyclic dermorphin‐related peptides reveals that the low‐energy structures contain tilted stacking interactions of the two aromatic residues Tyr1 and PHE3, and that this structural feature is a requirement for high μ receptor affinity.

a) a tilted stacking interaction of the Tyr1 and the Phe3 aromatic ring in the lowest or the second lowest energy conformers of the nine cyclic analogues is a structural requirement for a high affinity of the μ‐receptors, b) a low‐energy stacking arrangement of the aromatic rings is not possible for the four analogues which have poor affinity for the µ‐receptors, and c) the cyclic structures of the nine compounds are constrained, i.e., no more than four

1) the low energy conformations of the cyclic dermorphin analogue are all constrained and have a limited number of conformational families (five in total), and 2) the low energy conformational families with the best fit for the Tyr1 and Tyr4 aromatic rings are those that have a tilted stacking of these two rings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and biological evaluation of a series of cyclic dermorphins.
the synthesis and pharmacological characterization of cyclic peptides structurally related to dermorphin, a highly μ‐receptorspecific endogenous opioid.
the synthesis, conformational analysis, and pharmacological evaluation of cyclic analogues of the highly μ‐selective der morphin peptide,, which was synthesized by the solid‐phase method.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a conformational analysis based on molecular mechanics calculations is a valuable tool in the rational design of opioid peptides.
the μ‐receptors are not very selective in the conformation of the ligand.
a tilted stacking interaction is necessary but not sufficient to produce high μ‐receptors affinity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the μ‐receptors may have an aromatic stacking site in their binding site, and that the Tyr1–Phe3 stacking interaction is a necessary structural requirement for high affinity of the examined compounds for the μ‐site.
the μ‐receptors seem to prefer the Tyr1 and Tyr2 aromatic rings to be tilted with respect to each other, and that the Phe3 side‐chain is not involved in any specific interaction with the receptor.

the cyclic structure of dermorphin analogs is a prerequisite for high μ‐affinity, and that the presence of the aromatic rings of Tyr1 and Pher3 in a tilted stacking interaction may be a further requirement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while it may seem obvious that conformational changes in peptides could affect their bioactivities, it is often not so obvious how to go about studying the conformation‐bioactivity relationships.

the conformational analysis of these cyclic peptides, performed using a molecular mechanics force field, was able to identify a structural feature that is common to all analogues with high affinity for the μ opioid receptor.
the conformational flexibility of the exocytic residues Tyr1 and Pfe3 in these analogues is limited, and that the conformation of these two residues is crucial for the μ‐selective activity.
